_about: Make-row category 'Industrial' (Core/Tool/Shelf.cs; one file per category). Hide, never delete: type ids in hiddenTypes, style (preset) ids per type in hiddenStyles ({"park": ["pocket"]}), types moved in from another group in types. Hidden things keep their code and the game runner still builds them by id. Industrial (2026-10-19, the user: 'a whole new Industrial category ... industrial awesomeness ... like someone handcrafted it'): the handcrafted yards first (container yard, car yard, junk yard, industrial works: Core/Layers/Types/Industrial), then every type of the 'industrial' group that was hidden before (logistics yard, scrapyard, landfill, quarry, construction site, abandoned lot). The zoning type Industrial estate stays in Zoning (it zones lots; it does not build a yard). Makeover (2026-10-29/30, the user: fewer, better; every survivor A+): seen in the clean game (run show-42-builds-1029-232950-eebd), hidden what reads empty or as a grid there: the logistics yard and the old scrapyard (the container, car and junk yards do their work better), the junk yard reclaim (sparse goods on bare slabs) and tip and the works recycling (rows of identical skips), and every landfill but the active tip. The quarry came back (2026-10-30) rebuilt on the game's own pieces: open pit and abandoned shown; gravel and sand pits (flat empty floors) and the lake dig and flooded pit (no water surface in the clean game) hidden. The logistics yard stays hidden: its lattice spreads single small props over hectares under bright hatched bay decals; the container yard does stacked goods better.
